problem: The new doc comment of isLinkedWorktree says everything other than a linked worktree 'is copied as the base copy did', listing embedded clones, `.git` links and unreadable `.git` entries. The copy before this change did the opposite: the replaced isNestedCheckout skipped embedded clones, `.git` links and unreadable `.git` files ('skipping a directory is the safe way to be wrong'). So the comment describes a behaviour change as if it kept the old behaviour.
impact: A maintainer who trusts the comment thinks copying embedded clones and unreadable gitfiles is the old, settled behaviour. They will miss that this change reversed it, which matters when a test starts picking up a large embedded clone or a copy gets slower.
quote: Everything else is copied as the base copy did, because the tests may load it

problem: The dead-owner grace period ('two heartbeats') is a business rule. It appears as a bare `2 *` inside the abandonment expression. Its sibling threshold got a named constant (STALE_HEARTBEAT_MS) and an option, but this one did not. The tests then rebuild it by hand: `3 * HEARTBEAT_MS` at mutate.test.ts:365, 367, 381, 382 and more, and `2 * HEARTBEAT_MS ± 30_000` at mutate.test.ts:419-420. A local `staleButNotAbandoned` constant (mutate.test.ts:396) names it for one describe block only.
impact: Changing the grace means finding a bare multiplier in a ternary and about ten test literals that encode it indirectly. The docs (cli-reference, SKILL.detail, guide, review.ts help) also hard-code 'two minutes' and can drift silently.

problem: The new shared helper `make` takes five positional parameters with no options object. Two of them are adjacent, same-typed durations (directory age, then marker age). Call sites read `make(name, owner, 1000, 3 * HEARTBEAT_MS, repoScratch)`, so you cannot tell from the call which number ages what.
impact: If someone swaps ageMs and markerAgeMs in one of the 25+ calls, the test still compiles. It then exercises the 'unmarked and old' path instead of the 'stale marker' path, or the reverse, and passes for the wrong reason.
quote: async function make(name: string, owner: unknown, ageMs: number, markerAgeMs: number = ageMs, into: string = scratch)

problem: The same 'scan that aborts the turn, then resolves an open review' stub (new AbortController, a reviewGateState that calls controller.abort() and returns openReview()) is written out three times: at lines 165-171, 178-182 and 190-194. The file already pulled openReview into a helper but not the stub.
impact: Three copies of one scenario fixture. If the abort-during-scan setup changes (for example, aborting after the await instead of before it), all three must be edited the same way, or the LOGIC-003 tests quietly stop covering the TP-004 scenario.

problem: The file-type mask is written as the octal literal 0o170000 instead of the named `constants.S_IFMT` from node:fs. mutate.ts in the same change already imports `constants` for its O_* flags. The value ends up in every signature entry for a special file (`special:<type>`), which tests assert on.
impact: A reader has to recognise the POSIX S_IFMT mask by its digits to understand what goes into the signature.

problem: The parenthetical added to the treeHash sentence mixes two subjects: what treeHash leaves out (ignored files) and what the scratch copy leaves out. It reads as if linked worktrees were a kind of ignored file. It also names only one of the copy's exclusions; the mutate-scratch exclusion is stated in the next, new paragraph (lines 791-793), which says the copy rule again on its own. The mirror in src/gdskills/bundled/.../SKILL.detail.md has the same text.
impact: Readers of the review contract get the copy's exclusions in two places that partly overlap. Deleting the parenthetical and keeping the new paragraph would settle it.
quote: ignored files (the scratch copy still includes them, except linked worktrees, which it leaves out)
